A pallet gets several (the number above, 4 to start with), all with the same number: with 10 pallets and 4 labels each, Pallet 1 of 10 prints four times, then Pallet 2 of 10 four times, and so on. You can change all of this before printing.

twoFactor.title: Two-step verification
twoFactor.description: After your password, you type a 6-digit code from an authenticator app on your phone. Someone who finds out your password still cannot sign in.
twoFactor.statusOn: On: a code is asked after the password.
twoFactor.statusOff: Off: the password alone signs you in.
twoFactor.stepInstall: Install an authenticator app on your phone (Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator or similar).

twoFactor.stepType: Type the 6-digit code the app shows, then press Confirm.

password.title: Password
password.description: Change the password you sign in with. You stay signed in here; other places are signed out.

dashboard.title: Dashboard
dashboard.purpose: The factory at a glance: how much stock there is, in which warehouse, and which boxes have expired or are about to.
dashboard.steps:
The four tiles at the top show the total weight, the number of boxes, the number of different items and the boxes that need attention.
Press the tile “Need attention” to see every item that has expired or soon-to-expire boxes, and open an item to see its boxes.
Each warehouse has its own card: its weight, boxes and items, and a bar showing how many boxes are in date (green), expiring soon (amber) or expired (red).
Press the line “items need attention” on a card to see the items and boxes of that warehouse.
Press “Refresh data from Priority” to read the stock again now; otherwise it is read at most once a minute.
Press “Arrange the rooms” to put the warehouse cards in the order you want. The order is kept for you only: every person arranges their own.
dashboard.tips:
How many days before expiry counts as “soon” is set per category in System settings, under Receiving.
If Priority does not answer, nothing is lost: try again in a moment.

catalog.title: Item catalog
catalog.purpose: All the items from Priority. Look an item up here and print its label. Items are created and changed only in Priority.
catalog.steps:
Type a name (Hebrew or English), an item number or a barcode in the search box. The list narrows as you type.
Press a category card to see its items in a window. “All categories” shows everything.
Press an item to open its details: numbers, names, shelf life, storage text, package type and country of origin.
In the item window press “Print a label”: choose the label type, type the slaughter date and the production certificate number, check the country of origin and the copies, and press “Print”.
To print labels for many items at once press “Print several items”, tap the items, and press “Print labels”.
catalog.tips:
The expiry date on the label is calculated for you: the slaughter date plus the item’s shelf life.
The production certificate number is the number of the open order in Priority that the boxes will be received under.
If an item is weighed in a carton, choose its packaging in the item window (if you have permission); the receiving screen takes the packaging weight off.

receiving.title: Goods receiving
receiving.purpose: Receive the boxes made in the factory: scan the item label, put the box on the scale and save. The system saves the box, prints its label and sends it to Priority.
receiving.steps:
Scan the QR code on the item label in the scan box (the cursor is already there). The item, its dates and its certificate number fill in. Check them against the box.
No QR code? Press “No QR code: choose the item by hand”, find the item, and fill in the dates and the certificate number.
Put the box on the scale and wait until the display says “Stable”. If the scale is not connected, type the weight.
Press “Save and print label” (or press Enter). The box label prints and the box appears in today’s list.
In the list “Boxes received today” check that every box shows “Sent”. “Waiting” means Priority has not taken it yet and the system will try again by itself.
receiving.tips:
The production certificate number is the number of the open order in Priority that the box is received under.
Switch on “Print by itself about 2 seconds after the weight settles” to save and print without pressing anything.
Press “Reprint” next to a box to print its label again.

vendor.title: Vendor receiving
vendor.purpose: Receive boxes that come with the vendor’s own barcode (it starts with 38). No label is printed.
vendor.steps:
Scan the vendor barcode in the scan box, or type it and press Enter.
The system reads the item, the dates and the weight from the barcode, saves the box and sends it to Priority.
A green line shows what was received. The cursor stays in the scan box, so scan the next box right away: scans wait in line, so none is lost.
Listen to the sound: one high beep means recorded; two low beeps mean refused (the screen says why, for example already received); a long low buzz means the scan did not reach the system, and it is listed with a Retry button.
The list below shows today’s vendor boxes grouped by item. Use “Excel” or “Print” to take it out.
vendor.tips:
The speaker button next to the scan box turns the sounds off or on, on this computer only.
The list starts over every day at 21:00.
All vendor boxes are received under the vendor order chosen in System settings, under Receiving.

inventory.title: Inventory management
inventory.purpose: Every box that Priority holds in stock, down to the single box: filter, look, export reports and build pallets. It never changes stock.
inventory.steps:
Press a storage room card to see only that room. The first card shows all rooms.
Type an item number or name in the search box. Open “More filters” for the expiry status, a box barcode, and date ranges for expiry and entry.
Press an item to see its boxes beside it, the ones expiring first on top. Red means expired and amber means expiring soon.
Press “Export to Excel” or “Export to PDF” to take out exactly what the filters show.
Press “Build a pallet” to group boxes under one number (see the Pallets page).
inventory.tips:
“Entered” is the day the box was received in this system. For older stock it is the date Priority has.
The list shows 100 boxes at a time. Press “Show more” for the rest.

pallets.title: Pallets
pallets.purpose: Pallets: a fixed group of boxes under one number and one QR code. Making a pallet never changes stock.
pallets.steps:
Scan a pallet’s QR code, or type its number, to see every box on it.
For each box you see where it is now and when it expires. A box that left the stock is greyed and marked “Not in stock”.
Below, the latest pallets: press “Open” to see one, or “Print label” to print its label again.
To make a new pallet go back to the inventory and press “Build a pallet”.
pallets.tips: A pallet holds up to 500 boxes and can never be changed, so a printed number always means the same boxes.

settingsCompany.title: Company and labels
settingsCompany.purpose: The company logo, the label layouts and the shipping labels.
settingsCompany.steps:
Replace any of the three logos with “Upload new” (PNG, JPG or WebP, up to 1 MB). “Restore original” brings the first one back.
Press “Open the label designer” to design the item, box, pallet and shipping labels.
In the card “Shipping labels” press “Open the settings” to see the address that Priority sends picked orders to, to choose the label layout and the number of labels to start from, and to make a test order.
settingsCompany.tips:
Changes to a layout apply to the labels printed after you save it.
The address for Priority has a secret key inside it. “Make a new address” replaces the key; the old address then stops working.

settingsPriority.title: Priority
settingsPriority.purpose: How the system reaches Priority, and a practice mode for training.
settingsPriority.steps:
“Priority connection” shows the mode, the address, and whether a key and a password are saved. Press “Edit connection” to change them.
Press “Test connection” to check the connection.
“Priority data check” asks Priority which forms and fields it has. It only reads.
“Stand-in control” changes how the practice copy of Priority answers: normally, slowly, or not at all.
settingsPriority.tips:
The key and the password are stored encrypted and are never shown again.
In the live system, every box that is saved becomes a line in Priority.

settingsReceiving.title: Receiving
settingsReceiving.purpose: The rules for receiving: the vendor order, packaging types, expiry alerts, shelf life, storage rooms and the storage text on labels.
settingsReceiving.steps:
“Vendor receiving order”: choose the one Priority order that vendor boxes are received under, from the list or by typing any order number.
“Packaging type”: add the packagings and what one empty packaging weighs. Each item chooses one in the catalog.
For each category set the days to expiry (shelf life) and the alert days (how many days before expiry a box counts as expiring soon).
For each category choose the storage room and the storage text printed on its labels.
settingsReceiving.tips:
Each change is saved at once, with a short confirmation.
A box goes into the storage room named by its Priority order. The category’s room is used when the order names none.

settingsScale.title: Scale
settingsScale.purpose: Connect or disconnect the scale of this computer.
settingsScale.steps:
Close any other program that uses the scale (for example GetScale).
Press “Connect the scale”, choose the scale’s port in the browser’s window, and confirm.
The state changes to “Scale connected” and “Weight now” shows the live weight.
If the numbers look wrong open “Scale setup and what it sends” and change the speed or the reversed-numbers option.
Press “Disconnect the scale” to give the scale back to the old program.
settingsScale.tips: The scale works only in Chrome or Edge on a secure (https) address.

labels.title: Label layouts
labels.purpose: All the label layouts the system prints: item labels, the box label, the pallet label and shipping labels.
labels.steps:
Press “New layout”, choose a name, the kind and the size in millimetres, and press “Create and open”.
On each row the pencil opens a layout, the two squares duplicate it and the bin deletes it.
On an item layout, the star makes it the layout chosen first when printing.
Press a layout to design it in the label editor.
labels.tips: There is only one box label. The system needs a box layout to print box labels and a pallet layout to make pallets. Shipping labels are printed from the Shipping labels screen with the layout chosen in System settings.

labelEditor.title: Label designer
labelEditor.purpose: Design one label: its size and the things on it.
labelEditor.steps:
Under “Add to the label” press a button to put a text, a field (a value that changes with each label), a line, a box, a barcode, a QR code or a logo on the label.
Click an element on the label to select it. Drag it to move it and drag its handles to resize it.
The card “Selected element” has the exact position, size, typeface, bold, alignment and language of the text.
“Ready-made sections” adds a dates box, a warning box, the item names, or a complete box label in one press.
Press “Test print” to print the label on a page of its exact size, and “Save” (or Ctrl+S) to keep your changes.
labelEditor.tips:
Undo and Redo (Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Y) bring back what you changed.
Open “Show the keys” at the bottom for every keyboard shortcut.

adminUsers.title: Users
adminUsers.purpose: The people who can sign in, and what each one may see and do.
adminUsers.steps:
Press “New user”, type the name and the email (the email is the login and cannot be changed later) and choose the language.
For each screen choose “No access”, “View only” or “Everything”. Open the screen’s arrow to allow only single actions.
Choose the devices the person may use: a desktop computer, a phone, or both.
Press “Create user”. The system makes a temporary password and sends it by email with the sign-in link. It is also shown once on the screen.
The three dots on a person’s card open the actions: edit and permissions, reset the password, disable or enable, delete, and reset two-step verification.
adminUsers.tips:
The person chooses their own password the first time they sign in.
You can only give permissions that you have yourself.

adminLog.title: Activity log
adminLog.purpose: Everything that happens in the system, newest first. Entries can never be changed or deleted.
adminLog.steps:
Use “Filter the log” to choose a person, an action and a range of dates, and press “Show”.
Each row shows when, who, what, what it concerned and from which device.
Use the page buttons at the bottom to move between pages.
Press “Print report” to print or save a report of what the filter shows.

adminSends.title: Sends to Priority
adminSends.purpose: Boxes that Priority has not taken yet. Every box is saved first and then sent. This list shows the ones still waiting.
adminSends.steps:
If the list is empty, every box has reached Priority.
“Retrying” means Priority did not answer. The system tries again by itself, first after 30 seconds and then with longer breaks.
“Needs attention” means Priority refused the box. The reason is shown in the last column.
Fix the cause in Priority (for example the item, the storage room or the order), then press “Send again”, or “Send all again” for all of them.
adminSends.tips: Nothing is lost while a box waits here.

adminSecurity.title: Security
adminSecurity.purpose: Keep the system safe: warnings, who is signed in where, and the automatic sign-out.
adminSecurity.steps:
“Security warnings” lists attempts that look like someone trying to break in. Press “Mark as seen” when you have read them.
“Where people are signed in” lists every signed-in place with the person, the device, the address and the time. Press “Sign out” on a place you do not recognise.
“Automatic sign-out”: choose how long a person may leave the system untouched, and press “Save”.
adminSecurity.tips:
A red number on the menu means there are new warnings.
An account locked after 5 wrong passwords opens again by itself after 15 minutes.

account.title: My account
account.purpose: Your own password and two-step verification.
account.steps:
Press “Change password” to choose a new password. You stay signed in here; every other place is signed out.
Press “Turn on” to set up two-step verification: type your password, scan the picture with an authenticator app, and type the 6-digit code.
Save the backup codes in a safe place. Each works once, if you lose your phone.
account.tips: If you lose your phone and have no backup codes, ask the administrator to reset your two-step verification.

adminMessages.title: Messages
adminMessages.purpose: Questions, requests, problems and suggestions that people send from any page. Each one says exactly what it is about.
adminMessages.steps:
A red number on the Administration menu and on this tab shows how many new messages are waiting. A notice also appears when a new one arrives.
Each message shows its kind (question, request, problem or suggestion), the screen and the subject it is about, whether it is urgent, who sent it, from which device and when.
Read the person’s own words under it. “Sent from the page” shows the page they were on.
Type an answer if you want (the sender reads it under “Your messages” in the help window), and press “Mark as done”.
Use the buttons New, Answered and All to choose which messages are listed.
adminMessages.tips:
Urgent messages are always on top.
Every message and every answer is also written in the activity log.

shipping.title: Shipping labels
shipping.purpose: Labels for the boxes of an order, after the order was picked and confirmed in Priority. Nothing is picked or counted here.
shipping.steps:
When an order is picked and confirmed in Priority, Priority sends its details here and the order appears in the list.
Press “Print labels” on the order.
Choose Boxes or Pallets. A box gets one label. A pallet gets several labels (4 to start with), all with the same number.
Choose how many boxes or pallets, and for pallets how many labels for each. The window shows the label and the numbering: Box 1 of 10 up to Box 10 of 10, or Pallet 1 of 10 four times, then Pallet 2 of 10 four times, and so on.
Press Print. The labels come out in order, and the button shows how many there will be.
The list shows which orders were already printed and which are still waiting.
shipping.tips:
With 10 pallets and 4 labels for each, 40 labels print: 4 of each number.
Use the search box to find an order by its number, the customer or the city.
If Priority sends the same order again, it is updated in the list and can be printed again.
The address Priority needs, the layout, the number to start from and the labels for each pallet are set in System settings, under Company and labels.
